tags.gist: Says reliance on postmarket monitoring and voluntary developer disclosures both assume, without proof, that parties can detect their own failures.
Wants master file filers to disclose their internal detection methodology, not only claimed model behavior, so reviewers can judge the process.
Wants sponsors required to show positively how much their monitoring actually covers, since zero adverse events could mean monitoring saw nothing.
Wants degradation monitoring to include at least one detector outside the device's own reporting path, such as re-benchmarking or clinician review.
Frames its recommendations as supporting the framework, asking that monitoring and disclosure prove their reliability before earning premarket credit.
Argues this year's AI safety incidents show developers miss their own anomalies for months, so self-detection should not be load-bearing.
Since a model card discloses only what its filer already knows, wants referenced master files conditioned on revealing the filer's detection and monitoring methods.
Wants monitoring programs that justify reduced premarket evidence to document what share of interactions they capture and which behaviors fall outside their scope.
Wants at least one degradation detector, such as re-benchmarking on an independent set or sampled clinician review, outside the device's own output pathway.
Does not oppose postmarket reliance but wants monitoring and disclosure mechanisms to show completeness before being credited toward less premarket evidence.
